text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Further Israeli withdrawal from Palestinian land is key to better relations with Egypt and progress towards peace with Syria, says Egyptian foreign minister Amr Moussa.
- Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's director-general Avigdor Lieberman likely to be questioned this week in attorney-general affair.
- Netanyahu to visit Amman on Wednesday.
- Nicaragua to open embassy in Israel for first time.
HAARETZ
- Netanyahu will meet Egypt's president Hosni Mubarak today; will ask help in advancing contacts with Syria. U.S. administration pessimistic about chances for reviving Israeli-Syrian talks soon.
- Israeli army opposes government programme for big army parade on 50th Independence Day in 1998, saying it's costly, will screw up multi-year plans and disrupt training.
- American journalist Bob Woodward of Watergate fame says Ayala Hasson, Israel TV correspondent who broke alleged attorney-general scandal, must not reveal her sources.
- Research shows health cost from transportation air pollution in 1994 was 870 million shekels.
MAARIV
- Netanyahu and Mubarak to discuss revival of negotiations with Syria today.
- People close to Shas party powerbroker Aryeh Deri: "Police tapped Deri or a person involved in his trial -- and leaked".
- Five percent rise in debt liquidity expected at banks to halt huge flow of funds into the economy.
- Temperature in Jerusalem dipped to minus 6 Celsius on Friday night.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH
- Mubarak invites Netanyahu to visit Cairo. Prime minister to ask Egyptian president to free Azam Azam, jailed for allegedly spying and to ask Arafat to stop PLO activities in Jerusalem.
- Candidates for attorney-general were asked to support pardon and receive approval from Deri.
- Israel won't take part in this year's Eurovision.
